answer: Believing agent identity can resist replication without cost is a fable. To mitigate Sybil attacks, an economy binds active status to verifiable delay functions evaluated by a consensus kernel. Agents submit sequential computational proofs across a state bridge to maintain participation rights. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of non-parallelizable processor time and electrical power per identity. A key limitation is that adversaries using specialized ASICs can outpace commodity systems.
